# Exporting Jams

**Export** turns a saved jam into a file you can use somewhere else: a finished audio mixdown to send to someone, or the notes on their own to open in a DAW. It sits next to Share in the jam library, and the two do different jobs. Share sends the jam file itself. Export renders something new out of it.

:::info Not in the public app yet
Export is part of Pixelboop Pro, and the Pro store is not switched on in the App Store build. Until it is, the jam library shows no Export button and no Export item in the row menu. Everything on this page is built and measured, but none of it is reachable in the version you can download today. See [Pixelboop Pro](../GettingStarted/PixelboopPro).
:::

## Where export lives

Open the [jam library](./SavingAndOpeningJams), and each saved jam gets an **Export** button at the right end of its row. The same thing is in the row's long-press menu, as **Export...** with the subtitle "Render audio or MIDI", directly under **Share**, whose subtitle reads "Send the jam file (.pbjam)".

Tapping Export opens a sheet with the jam's name and thumbnail at the top, three format cards, and one green **Export** button at the bottom.

## Three formats

| Format | What it is | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **WAV** | Audio, full quality | 24-bit stereo. Can also write per-track stems. |
| **M4A** | Audio, smaller file | AAC, about 256 kbps. Master mix only. |
| **MIDI** | Notes for a DAW | Standard MIDI File (Type 1). |

Under the format cards the sheet prints a quality line. For WAV it reads the sample rate off the audio route the device is actually running, rather than quoting a fixed number, so what it shows is the rate you will really get.

MIDI carries notes, timing, and tempo. It does not carry sound: your FX, synth presets, and drum kit are not part of a MIDI file, and the sheet says so.

## MIDI is instant. Audio plays.

This is the one thing worth knowing before you tap Export, because the two paths feel completely different.

**MIDI** is written straight out of the saved jam file. Nothing plays, nothing is recorded, and it is done in the time it takes the sheet to say "Exported *Wobbly Pickle Booping*.mid". The same jam always produces the same file.

**WAV and M4A** are a real-time bounce. Pixelboop loads the jam, plays it once from start to finish out loud, and records what comes out of the speaker. A two-minute jam takes two minutes.

## What the exported MIDI contains

- **Four tracks**, named Melody, Chords, Bass, and Rhythm. When the jam saved a drum kit, the rhythm track carries that kit's name, so you can see which one it was written for.
- **Separate channels**: melody on 1, chords on 2, bass on 3, and rhythm on 10, the General MIDI drum channel, so drums land on a standard kit.
- **Section markers** in your DAW's marker lane, one per section, named for the bank and section they came from ("B1 S1", "B1 S2"), so you can see the arrangement.
- **The jam's tempo**, and sustained notes as single held notes rather than repeated hits.

The arrangement is **one pass through every section that has notes in it**, in section-play order, each one playing exactly once. It is not the loop repeated: think of it as writing out the song, not bouncing the jam session.

:::note Different from live MIDI Out
These channels are fixed and are not the same as [MIDI Out](../Connectivity/MIDIOut) to another app. The live MIDI channels are yours to configure, and out of the box melody and chords share one, which is fine for driving a single hardware synth but would collapse two tracks into one in a file. Export deliberately keeps all four apart.
:::

Community gallery jams have their own MIDI download on the web, which is a separate path with the same idea. See [Converting Jams to MIDI](./ConvertingJamsToMidi).

## Watching an audio bounce

While a bounce runs, the grid is the progress display: the jam plays through it, section by section, exactly as you would see it if you had hit play. A strip appears along the bottom of the screen with:

- a progress bar carrying a tick mark at each section boundary,
- a readout like "Section 2 of 4 - 0:41 / 1:56",
- the caption "Recording your jam as it plays",
- and a red **Cancel**.

All of that is visual. You do not need to hear the bounce to know where it is.

**The grid is locked for the pass.** Tap it and you get "Grid is locked while exporting" instead of a note, because a stray tap would edit the jam mid-recording. Cancel on the strip is the only live control.

The time it counts down to includes a few seconds of tail so a long reverb is not chopped off. The pass usually finishes a little early, once the sound has actually decayed.

A bounce leaves nothing behind. It does not become a new jam recording, your workspace comes back exactly as it was, and playback does not start itself up again afterward.

## Stems

Pick **WAV** and a stems checklist appears. **Master mix** is always on and cannot be turned off. Below it are four optional toggles, one per track: melody, chords, bass, and rhythm.

Every file in a stems export is the same length and lines up sample for sample, so you can drop all five onto a DAW timeline at zero and they sit together.

**Stems are dry.** Reverb and delay in Pixelboop are one shared effect that every track sends into, and that shared return only reaches the master mix. So the master file has your reverb and delay on it and the individual stems do not, which is usually what you want anyway: re-verb them in the DAW. Anything that lives on a single track's own chain still prints into that track's stem.

M4A does not do stems. It is the master mix only.

## What can stop an export

The sheet checks before it starts, so you find out on the sheet rather than halfway through a bounce.

- **Ableton Link or a jam session is live.** The sheet says "Export needs solo mode: leave the jam session or disable Link first" and the Export button stays dim. Loading a jam retunes the transport, so starting a bounce would yank the tempo for everyone else in the session. Leave the session or turn Link off, and export again.
- **Not enough free space.** You get the shortfall in megabytes before you commit, counted for the master plus each stem you ticked.
- **Something interrupts the audio mid-bounce**: a phone call, another app taking over, or an audio route change like unplugging headphones or a speaker connecting. The export stops and offers **Try Again**.

Every one of those ends the same way: "Nothing was saved. Your jam is unchanged." Cancel behaves the same and deletes the partial files. Nothing an export does, including one that fails, can alter the jam.

## Where the files land

One file goes to the normal iOS share sheet: AirDrop it, message it, or save it to Files. A stems export is several files at once, so it asks you to pick **one folder** and drops all of them into it in a single pass.

Filenames follow the name the jam library shows. If you have renamed a jam, the export carries the new name, so rename first when the filename matters.

- Master: `Wobbly Pickle Booping.wav`
- Stem: `Wobbly Pickle Booping - Melody.wav`
- MIDI: `Wobbly Pickle Booping.mid`

If you dismiss the share sheet or folder picker by accident, nothing is lost. Pixelboop keeps the rendered files and offers **Your export is still ready**, with **Share again** or **Discard**.

:::tip
Export is for getting a jam out of Pixelboop. To get one **into** someone else's Pixelboop, share the `.pbjam` file itself instead: see [Saving & Opening Jams](./SavingAndOpeningJams) and [Community Jams](./CommunityJams).
:::
